description: In Jewish tradition, the number eighteen represents life. The Hebrew letters chet (ח=8) and jod (י=10) together form the word chai (חי), which means 'living'. This connection between the number and the concept of life is deeply rooted in Jewish thought, where life is understood as God's supreme gift. Chai points to the life-giving power that flows from God – the same life force described in the Torah as "the tree of life" (ets chaim). The number 18 therefore carries within it a fundamental affirmation of the holiness of life and God's enduring care for His creation.

footnotes.text: It is common in Jewish culture to give gifts in multiples of 18 (18, 36, 54, etc.) as a symbolic expression of blessing and life. This custom is often referred to as giving "l'chaim" – to life.

Shemoneh Esreh (שמונה עשרה, 'the eighteen') is one of the most central prayers in Jewish liturgy, also known as Amidah ('the standing'). Originally it consisted of eighteen blessings, but a nineteenth was added in early rabbinic times. Despite this addition, the prayer retained the name 'the eighteen'.

In Kabbalistic thought, chai is associated with the life force (chiyyut) that sustains all creation. The letters chet and yod are seen as channels for divine energy flowing down through the sefirot system.
